phrases.translation: Glory be to the One Who took His servant ˹Muḥammad˺ by night from the Sacred Mosque to the Farthest Mosque
phrases.explanation: God declares Himself far above every shortcoming and any false claim made about Him as He recalls taking His Servant Muhammad by night from the Sacred Mosque in Mecca to the Farthest Mosque in Jerusalem. Early authorities differed on whether he traveled in body and soul upon the mount called al-Buraq or whether the journey was shown to his spirit, though most held that God carried his person there in a single night.

phrases.translation: whose surroundings We have blessed, so that We may show him some of Our signs.
phrases.explanation: The land surrounding the Farthest Mosque in Syria and Jerusalem was blessed by God with flowing rivers, fruit-bearing trees, abundant crops, and the dwelling places of earlier prophets. God carried His Servant there by night so that he might behold miraculous signs of divine power, including the prophetic gathering and the great wonders of the heavens and the earth that confirmed his mission and strengthened his heart.

phrases.translation: Indeed, He alone is the All-Hearing, All-Seeing
phrases.explanation: God hears every word spoken by His Servant and by those who either believe or deny his report of the night journey, and He sees all that they do in secret and in open view. Nothing in the heavens or the earth escapes His perception, so He rewards the truthful believers and holds the stubborn deniers accountable for their mockery.

phrases.translation: And We gave Moses the Scripture and made it a guide for the Children of Israel,
phrases.explanation: Just as God honored Muhammad with the night journey and the revelation of the Quran, He previously gave Moses the Torah and made it a light and clear guidance for the Children of Israel. Through that revealed scripture He led them out of error and showed them the straight path of obedience, worship, and lawful conduct in their lives.

phrases.translation: ˹stating:˺ “Do not take besides Me any other Trustee of Affairs
phrases.explanation: The core charge set forth inside the scripture given to Moses was that the Children of Israel should never take any lord, protector, or trustee of affairs besides God alone. Whether read in the canonical recitations as a direct prohibition against taking another guardian or as a statement of purpose, it obligates complete reliance upon God without any partner.

phrases.translation: ˹O˺ descendants of those We carried with Noah ˹in the Ark˺!
phrases.explanation: The Children of Israel are addressed here as the offspring of those whom God rescued and carried aboard the ark with Noah during the great flood when the rest of humanity drowned. Reminding them of how their ancestors were saved by God's grace calls them to show the same devotion and single-minded trust in their Lord alone.

phrases.translation: He was indeed a grateful servant.”
phrases.explanation: Noah was a deeply grateful servant who praised and thanked God whenever he ate, drank, put on a garment, or rose and lay down, acknowledging every single blessing as coming purely from his Lord. His descendants are urged to imitate their righteous forefather by thanking God through pure monotheism and steadfast obedience.

phrases.translation: And We warned the Children of Israel in the Scripture, “You will certainly cause corruption in the land twice, and you will become extremely arrogant
phrases.explanation: God made a firm, foreordained decree and revealed it clearly to the Children of Israel in the scripture written for them, warning them in advance that they would rebel against Him and spread corruption in the holy land of Jerusalem and Syria on two separate occasions. Through bloodshed, disobedience, and violating the rulings of the Torah, they would exalt themselves with extreme arrogance over people and against their Lord.

phrases.translation: When the first of the two warnings would come to pass, We would send against you some of Our servants of great might, who would ravage your homes.
phrases.explanation: When the appointed time of punishment arrived for the first of their two rebellions, after they violated the Torah and killed or persecuted prophets such as Isaiah, Jeremiah, or Zechariah, God raised against them fierce warriors of immense military strength who marched through the interiors of their homes to slay the fighters and take captives. Early authorities variously identified these invaders as Goliath, Sennacherib of Mosul, or Nebuchadnezzar of Babylon.

phrases.translation: This would be a warning fulfilled
phrases.explanation: This devastating invasion and ransacking of their dwellings was an inescapable divine promise and foreordained decree that had to be fulfilled. Once they persisted in flagrant transgression, bloodshed, and killing the prophets sent to them, nothing could avert the humiliating judgment that God had written against them in their own scripture.

phrases.translation: Then ˹after your repentance˺ We would give you the upper hand over them and aid you with wealth and offspring, causing you to outnumber them
phrases.explanation: After the Children of Israel repented and set their affairs right, God restored their sovereignty and gave them the upper hand over their enemies, whether by David slaying Goliath or by their return from Babylonian captivity. He replenished their lost wealth and grain, multiplied their children, and made their fighting men more numerous and powerful than before.

phrases.translation: If you act rightly, it is for your own good, but if you do wrong, it is to your own loss.
phrases.explanation: God reminded them that if they acted rightly by obeying His commands and keeping His covenant, the reward and benefit of that obedience would return entirely to their own souls. Conversely, if they did wrong and returned to disobedience, the harm and punishment of that sin would fall back upon themselves alone without hurting God in the least.

phrases.translation: “And when the second warning would come to pass, your enemies would ˹be left to˺ totally disgrace you
phrases.explanation: When the Children of Israel rebelled a second time by shedding sacred blood and killing the prophet John the Baptist, the appointed time of the second warning arrived. God sent foreign conquerors such as Nebuchadnezzar or Antiochian kings to humiliate them so severely that grief, terror, and total disgrace darkened their faces.

phrases.translation: and enter the Temple ˹of Jerusalem˺ as they entered it the first time, and utterly destroy whatever would fall into their hands
phrases.explanation: The invaders stormed into the Sacred Temple in Jerusalem just as the earlier army had entered it during the first rebellion, slaughtering its defenders and plundering its treasures. Everything they conquered and gained mastery over across the city and its sanctuaries was laid waste with complete ruin and utter destruction.

phrases.translation: Perhaps your Lord will have mercy on you ˹if you repent˺, but if you return ˹to sin˺, We will return ˹to punishment˺.
phrases.explanation: God held out hope that after their second affliction their Lord would show them mercy and restore their state if they sincerely repented. Yet He warned that if they ever returned to corruption and disobedience, He would return to punishing them, a warning fulfilled when they rejected Muhammad and faced defeat, exile, and the payment of tribute.

phrases.translation: And We have made Hell a ˹permanent˺ confinement for the disbelievers.”
phrases.explanation: Beyond the humiliations and punishments of this worldly life, God has made Hell an inescapable prison and permanent confinement in the Hereafter for those who disbelieve in Him and reject His scriptures. There they are held fast and surrounded on every side by torment with no way of release.

phrases.translation: Surely this Quran guides to what is most upright,
phrases.explanation: This Quran guides humanity to the path that is straightest, most upright, and most just, namely confessing the oneness of God and obeying His messengers. Unlike the crooked paths of polytheism and error, its revealed teachings direct people to what is soundest in belief, character, and action.

phrases.translation: and gives good news to the believers—who do good—that they will have a mighty reward
phrases.explanation: At the same time, the Quran brings joyful news to those who truly believe in God and His Messenger and confirm their inward faith by performing righteous deeds and avoiding sin. It promises them an immense, lasting reward from their Lord in the eternal gardens of Paradise.

phrases.translation: And ˹it warns˺ those who do not believe in the Hereafter ˹that˺ We have prepared for them a painful punishment
phrases.explanation: Alongside its glad tidings for the righteous believers, the Quran also warns those who deny the resurrection after death and refuse to believe in the accountability of the Hereafter. For such deniers, God has already prepared an agonizing torment in the Fire of Hell as a just recompense for their rejection of the truth.

phrases.translation: And humans ˹swiftly˺ pray for evil as they pray for good. For humankind is ever hasty
phrases.explanation: In moments of anger, impatience, or distress, a person swiftly invokes curses of ruin, death, or poverty against himself, his children, or his wealth just as eagerly as he prays for health and prosperity. Human beings are by nature hasty and restless, demanding immediate outcomes without weighing what would happen if God actually answered their rash prayers.

phrases.translation: We made the day and night as two signs. So We made the sign of the night devoid of light, and We made the sign of the day ˹perfectly˺ bright,
phrases.explanation: God established the alternation of night and day as two great signs of His power, darkening the sign of the night for rest and making the sign of the day bright so people can see clearly. Early authorities also explained that the moon was once as bright as the sun before God blotted out its light, leaving the dark marks seen on the moon.

phrases.translation: so that you may seek the bounty of your Lord and know the number of years and calculation ˹of time˺. And We have explained everything in detail
phrases.explanation: Bright daylight enables people to go out and seek livelihood and provision from their Lord, while the regular cycles of night and day and the phases of the moon allow them to count the passing days, months, and years. In the same way, God has explained every necessary matter clearly and in detail in His revelation.

phrases.translation: We have bound every human’s destiny to their neck.
phrases.explanation: Using the Arab image of a bird of omen, the verse declares that every person's true destiny toward happiness or misery, along with every good or evil deed he performs, is bound inseparably to his neck like a collar. Nothing happens by random luck, for each soul carries its own decreed record wherever it goes.

phrases.translation: And on the Day of Judgment We will bring forth to each ˹person˺ a record which they will find laid open
phrases.explanation: On the Day of Judgment, God will bring forth all those recorded deeds in a written book that each person will meet laid wide open before his eyes. Every righteous action and every sin he committed throughout his life will be inscribed inside it without the slightest omission.

phrases.translation: ˹And it will be said,˺ “Read your record. You ˹alone˺ are sufficient this Day to take account of yourself.”
phrases.explanation: It will be said to him on that Day to read his own book of deeds, and every person will read his record clearly even if he never knew how to read in the world. Because every secret and public act is recorded truthfully, his own soul suffices as a witness and reckoner against him, leaving no room to claim injustice.

phrases.translation: Whoever chooses to be guided, it is only for their own good. And whoever chooses to stray, it is only to their own loss.
phrases.explanation: Whoever chooses to follow the straight path of faith and obeys the Messenger does so solely for the salvation, reward, and benefit of his own soul. Conversely, whoever chooses to stray from the truth harms only himself, bearing the full burden and penalty of his own misguidance before God.

phrases.translation: No soul burdened with sin will bear the burden of another. And We would never punish ˹a people˺ until We have sent a messenger ˹to warn them˺
phrases.explanation: No sinful soul will ever be made to carry the guilt of another person's sins, for each individual is held accountable only for his own actions. Furthermore, out of perfect justice, God never destroys or punishes any people until He first sends a messenger to warn them and remove every excuse.

phrases.translation: Whenever We intend to destroy a society, We command its elite ˹to obey Allah˺ but they act rebelliously in it.
phrases.explanation: When the appointed time approaches for God to destroy a wicked society, He commands its wealthy elite to obey Him and follow His messenger, though they rebel instead. In variant readings and early interpretations, the verb also means that He makes its affluent elites rulers over the city or multiplies their numbers and luxury.

phrases.translation: So the decree ˹of punishment˺ is justified, and We destroy it utterly
phrases.explanation: Because those privileged leaders commit flagrant rebellion, tyranny, and corruption inside the town instead of obeying God, the decree of punishment becomes fully justified and binding upon the community. God then annihilates the city utterly, sweeping away its inhabitants and structures so that nothing of its former power remains.

phrases.translation: ˹Imagine˺ how many peoples We have destroyed after Noah!
phrases.explanation: After the flood of Noah, God destroyed countless generations of disbelieving nations such as Ad and Thamud who rejected their messengers despite having been granted far greater wealth and strength. Their fate serves as a stern warning to the Quraysh that rejecting Muhammad brings the very same ruin.

phrases.translation: And sufficient is your Lord as All-Aware and All-Seeing of the sins of His servants
phrases.explanation: Your Lord alone suffices as One who is fully aware of every hidden sin of His servants and who sees all their open transgressions without needing any informant. Nothing they do escapes His notice, and He will repay each of them in full according to His justice.

phrases.translation: Whoever desires this fleeting world ˹alone˺, We hasten in it whatever We please to whoever We will;
phrases.explanation: If a person desires only the fleeting pleasures of this immediate worldly life, even performing deeds that appear righteous merely for worldly gain without seeking the Hereafter, God hastens for him only as much earthly provision as He pleases and only for whomever He wills, rather than giving everything the seeker craves.

phrases.translation: then We destine them for Hell, where they will burn, condemned and rejected
phrases.explanation: After his brief enjoyment of the world comes to an end, God destines him for Hell in the Hereafter, where he will enter to burn in its flames. He will arrive there condemned and blamed for wasting his life in ingratitude, rejected and driven far away from divine mercy.

phrases.translation: But whoever desires the Hereafter and strives for it accordingly, and is a ˹true˺ believer, it is they whose striving will be appreciated
phrases.explanation: By contrast, whoever longs for the eternal reward of the Hereafter and strives for it as it deserves by fulfilling God's commands and avoiding sin while holding true faith in Him and His promise will find his striving accepted. God appreciates their effort by forgiving their slips and rewarding their good deeds generously.

phrases.translation: We provide both the former and the latter from the bounty of your Lord. And the bounty of your Lord can never be withheld
phrases.explanation: In this world, God extends His material provision and sustenance to both groups alike, granting livelihood to those who seek the fleeting world and to the believers who seek the Hereafter. The bounty of your Lord in earthly provision is never withheld or barred from anyone, whether obedient or rebellious.

phrases.translation: See how We have favoured some over others ˹in this life˺, but the Hereafter is certainly far greater in rank and in favour
phrases.explanation: Observe how God has favored some people over others in this world with greater wealth, ease, or spiritual insight. Yet the Hereafter features far greater ranks and far wider distinctions in favor, where believers are elevated to lofty stations in Paradise according to their deeds while disbelievers sink into everlasting ruin.

phrases.translation: Do not set up any other god with Allah, or you will end up condemned, abandoned
phrases.explanation: Addressed directly to the Prophet and through him to every accountable human being, this command forbids setting up any partner alongside God in worship. Whoever associates another deity with God will end up condemned for betraying his true Benefactor and abandoned without any helper to defend him when God forsakes him.

phrases.translation: For your Lord has decreed that you worship none but Him. And honour your parents.
phrases.explanation: Your Lord has commanded and decreed as a binding religious duty that you worship none but Him alone, reserving divinity exclusively for Him, and immediately after pure devotion to Him He has joined the command to honor one's father and mother with unfailing kindness, respect, and dutiful care.

phrases.translation: If one or both of them reach old age in your care, never say to them ˹even˺ ‘ugh,’ nor yell at them. Rather, address them respectfully
phrases.explanation: When one or both parents grow frail, weak, and dependent in old age under your care, you must bear their needs patiently just as they cared for you in infancy. Never utter even the slightest grunt of annoyance or yell at them, but instead address them with gentle, respectful, and honoring speech.

phrases.translation: And be humble with them out of mercy, and pray, “My Lord! Be merciful to them as they raised me when I was young.”
phrases.explanation: Like a bird folding its wings gently over its young, a believer must humble himself before his parents out of tender mercy, never refusing them anything they wish so long as it involves no sin. Along with outward kindness, he should pray for God to have mercy on them just as they tirelessly raised him when he was small.

phrases.translation: Your Lord knows best what is within yourselves.
phrases.explanation: God knows best what lies hidden inside your hearts regarding your parents, whether it is sincere reverence, mercy, and affection or concealed irritation, contempt, and disrespect. Nothing in the breast is hidden from Him, and He judges and rewards people according to their true inward intent.

phrases.translation: If you are righteous, He is certainly All-Forgiving to those who ˹constantly˺ turn to Him
phrases.explanation: If you are sincerely righteous and dutiful toward your parents at heart, then even if a sudden slip, unguarded impulse, or hasty word escapes you without malice, God is certainly All-Forgiving to those who constantly turn back to Him in repentance, regret their mistake, and mend their conduct.

phrases.translation: Give to close relatives their due, as well as the poor and ˹needy˺ travellers.
phrases.explanation: Fulfill the duty owed to close relatives by maintaining family ties, showing kindness, and supporting them in need, and likewise give charitable help from your wealth to the destitute poor who go without and to the needy traveler who is stranded far from his home and resources.

phrases.translation: And do not spend wastefully
phrases.explanation: While commanding generosity toward relatives and the needy, God forbids squandering wealth wastefully. Early authorities stressed that spending even a single coin in disobedience to God or on unlawful things is wasteful extravagance, whereas spending everything one owns in obedience to God and His cause is never considered waste.

phrases.translation: Surely the wasteful are ˹like˺ brothers to the devils. And the Devil is ever ungrateful to his Lord
phrases.explanation: Those who squander their wealth in sin and disobedience to God are called brothers to the devils because they follow Satan's rule and will share his company in the Fire. Just as the Devil was utterly ungrateful for the favors of his Lord, the wasteful misuse God's blessings against His command.

phrases.translation: But if you must turn them down ˹because you lack the means to give˺—while hoping to receive your Lord’s bounty—then ˹at least˺ give them a kind word
phrases.explanation: When relatives or needy people ask for help and you must turn them down because you have nothing on hand to give them, while waiting and hoping to receive future bounty from your Lord, do not rebuke them. Instead, decline them politely with a kind, gentle promise that you will give once God provides.

phrases.translation: Do not be so tight-fisted, for you will be blameworthy; nor so open-handed, for you will end up in poverty
phrases.explanation: God forbids two extremes in handling wealth: do not be so tight-fisted, as if your hand were chained to your neck, that you refuse to spend in God's cause and become blameworthy for miserliness, nor so open-handed that you give away everything you own and end up sitting in poverty and regret.

phrases.translation: Surely your Lord gives abundant or limited provisions to whoever He wills. He is certainly All-Aware, All-Seeing of His servants
phrases.explanation: People should neither hoard out of fear nor squander recklessly, because it is your Lord who gives abundant provision to whomever He wills and limits it for whomever He wills according to His wisdom. He is fully aware of His servants' needs and sees which measure of wealth suits each person best.

phrases.translation: Do not kill your children for fear of poverty. We provide for them and for you. Surely killing them is a heinous sin
phrases.explanation: God strictly forbids the pre-Islamic pagan practice of burying daughters alive out of dread that feeding them would bring poverty and destitution. He reminds parents that He alone provides sustenance both for the children and for the parents themselves, and that slaying one's offspring is a heinous sin and grave transgression.

phrases.translation: Do not go near adultery. It is truly a shameful deed and an evil way
phrases.explanation: Believers are commanded not even to come near adultery and fornication or the temptations that lead to it. Such unlawful sexual conduct is a vile, shameful abomination and an evil way because it violates God's law, corrupts lineages, and leads its perpetrator straight to the punishment of Hell.

phrases.translation: Do not take a ˹human˺ life—made sacred by Allah—except with ˹legal˺ right.
phrases.explanation: God forbids taking any human life that He has made sacred, whether a believer or a person protected by a covenant, except with legal right established by divine justice, such as lawful retribution for intentional murder, execution for adultery after lawful marriage, or apostasy and warring against faith.

phrases.translation: If anyone is killed unjustly, We have given their heirs the authority, but do not let them exceed limits in retaliation, for they are already supported ˹by law˺
phrases.explanation: When someone is killed unjustly, God grants the victim's heirs legal authority to demand retribution, accept blood-money, or pardon the killer. Yet the heir must not exceed limits in retaliation by killing anyone other than the actual murderer or mutilating him, as pagan Arabs used to do, for God and the law already support his right.

phrases.translation: Do not come near the wealth of the orphan—unless intending to enhance it—until they attain maturity.
phrases.explanation: Guardians are forbidden to touch an orphan's wealth unless intending to preserve and grow it for the child's benefit, although a poor guardian who manages the estate may eat from it reasonably without extravagance. Once the orphan reaches physical maturity and sound judgment, his property must be handed over to him.

phrases.translation: Honour ˹your˺ pledges, for you will surely be accountable for them
phrases.explanation: Every lawful pledge, contract, and covenant made between people in God's name must be honored faithfully and never betrayed. On the Day of Judgment, God will call every person to account for his pledges and question him directly about whether he fulfilled them honestly or broke them.

phrases.translation: Give in full when you measure, and weigh with an even balance. That is fairest and best in the end
phrases.explanation: In all commercial dealings, sellers must give full measure without stinting and weigh goods with an upright, even balance that neither cheats nor shortchanges the buyer. Honesty in measure and weight is fairest for people in this world and brings the best reward from God in the end.

phrases.translation: Do not follow what you have no ˹sure˺ knowledge of.
phrases.explanation: Do not pursue, testify, or make accusations about matters of which you have no sure knowledge, such as claiming to have seen what you did not see, claiming to have heard what you did not hear, or slandering innocent people on the basis of mere guesswork and suspicion.

phrases.translation: Indeed, all will be called to account for ˹their˺ hearing, sight, and intellect
phrases.explanation: On the Day of Resurrection, every person will be called to account for how he used his hearing, sight, and intellect, and the faculties themselves will bear witness concerning what the ear listened to, what the eye looked at, and what the heart and mind intended or believed.

phrases.translation: And do not walk on the earth arrogantly. Surely you can neither crack the earth nor stretch to the height of the mountains
phrases.explanation: God forbids strutting across the earth with haughty pride, vanity, and arrogance. No matter how fiercely an arrogant person stamps his feet, he is far too weak to crack the ground beneath him, and no matter how proudly he stretches his neck, he will never reach the height of the mountains.

phrases.translation: The violation of any of these ˹commandments˺ is detestable to your Lord
phrases.explanation: Looking back over all the moral commandments and prohibitions set forth from the decree to worship God alone down to the ban on arrogance, God declares that the violation of any of these rulings is hateful, displeasing, and detestable in the sight of your Lord, who forbids all evil.

phrases.translation: This is part of the wisdom which your Lord has revealed to you ˹O Prophet˺.
phrases.explanation: All these noble moral teachings, virtuous duties, and clear prohibitions that have just been set forth are part of the divine wisdom that your Lord has revealed to you in the Quran, instructing humanity how to live uprightly in justice and avoid the paths of ruin.

phrases.translation: And do not set up any other god with Allah ˹O humanity˺, or you will be cast into Hell, blameworthy, rejected
phrases.explanation: The passage closes just as it began by warning every accountable person never to set up another god alongside God in worship. Whoever commits polytheism will be cast into the flames of Hell, blameworthy before his own soul and creation, and rejected far away from all good.

phrases.translation: Has your Lord favoured you ˹pagans˺ with sons and taken angels as ˹His˺ daughters? You are truly making an outrageous claim
phrases.explanation: Rebuking the Arab pagans who claimed that the angels were God's daughters, the verse asks how they can imagine that their Lord favored them exclusively with sons while taking angels as daughters for Himself, when they despised daughters and buried them alive. Truly, they utter an outrageous, monstrous lie against God.

phrases.translation: We have surely varied ˹the signs˺ in this Quran so perhaps they may be mindful, but it only drives them farther away
phrases.explanation: God has presented every kind of sign, parable, warning, and lesson in varied ways throughout this Quran so that people might reflect upon their error and become mindful. Yet instead of awakening the stubborn polytheists, these clear reminders only drive them farther away from the truth in aversion.

phrases.translation: Say, ˹O Prophet,˺ “Had there been other gods besides Him—as they claim—then they would have certainly sought a way to ˹challenge˺ the Lord of the Throne.”
phrases.explanation: Tell the polytheists that if there actually were other deities besides God as they falsely claim, those lesser gods would themselves have sought a way to the Lord of the Mighty Throne, either by striving to draw near to Him in humble obedience, as most authorities explained, or by seeking to challenge Him for dominion.

phrases.translation: Glorified and Highly Exalted is He above what they claim
phrases.explanation: God declares His absolute purity and transcends every false claim of partners, rivals, or female offspring that the polytheists fabricate against Him. He is glorified and infinitely exalted in majesty, power, and sovereignty far above all the slanders and lies that they attribute to Him.

phrases.translation: The seven heavens, the earth, and all those in them glorify Him.
phrases.explanation: Out of awe and reverence for His majesty, the seven heavens, the earth, and all believers within them among the angels, humans, and jinn glorify God with constant praise and declare Him utterly free of the partners, rivals, and female offspring that the polytheists invent against Him.

phrases.translation: There is not a single thing that does not glorify His praises—but you ˹simply˺ cannot comprehend their glorification. He is indeed Most Forbearing, All-Forgiving
phrases.explanation: Every created thing in existence glorifies God with His praises, whether early authorities understood this literally of all living and inanimate things, such as creaking doors, trees, and flowing water, or specifically of living creatures, though human beings cannot comprehend their languages of praise. Despite humanity's sins, God remains Most Forbearing and All-Forgiving.

phrases.translation: When you ˹O Prophet˺ recite the Quran, We put a hidden barrier between you and those who do not believe in the Hereafter
phrases.explanation: Whenever the Prophet recites the Quran to those who deny the Resurrection and do not believe in the Hereafter, God places a hidden barrier between him and their hearts. Because they persisted in arrogance and disbelief, this spiritual veil prevents them from grasping or benefiting from the guidance recited to them.

phrases.translation: We have cast veils over their hearts—leaving them unable to comprehend it—and deafness in their ears.
phrases.explanation: As a consequence of their stubborn rejection of the truth, God has cast thick veils over the hearts of the deniers so that they remain unable to comprehend the Quran, and a heavy deafness in their ears so that they do not truly hear and benefit from its message.

phrases.translation: And when you mention your Lord alone in the Quran, they turn their backs in aversion
phrases.explanation: Whenever you proclaim in the Quran that there is no deity except your Lord alone without mentioning their idols and false gods alongside Him, the polytheists recoil in disgust and turn their backs to flee in aversion, offended that divinity and worship should be reserved exclusively for God.

phrases.translation: We know best how they listen to your recitation and what they say privately—when the wrongdoers say, “You would only be following a bewitched man.”
phrases.explanation: God knows full well the scornful intent with which the Meccan leaders listen to your recitation of the Quran and what they whisper in their private councils, when the polytheistic wrongdoers tell one another that anyone who follows Muhammad is only following a man bewitched by magic or a mere mortal who eats and drinks.

phrases.translation: See how they call you names ˹O Prophet˺! So they have gone so ˹far˺ astray that they cannot find the ˹Right˺ Way
phrases.explanation: Consider how your opponents invent contradictory names and comparisons for you, calling you a bewitched man, a sorcerer, a poet, or a soothsayer. By fabricating these false labels they have wandered so far astray from the truth that they cannot find any way to guidance or salvation.

phrases.translation: And they say ˹mockingly˺, “When we are reduced to bones and ashes, will we really be raised as a new creation?”
phrases.explanation: Mocking the promise of the Hereafter out of stubborn denial, the Meccan polytheists ask in disbelief how they could possibly be raised back to life as a brand-new creation after they have died and their bodies have decayed in the graves into dry bones and finely crushed dust and ashes.

phrases.translation: Say, ˹O Prophet,˺ “˹Yes, even if˺ you become stones, or iron
phrases.explanation: God instructs the Prophet to answer their scoffing by challenging them directly: yes, you will be raised even if, instead of soft flesh and decaying bone, you could turn yourselves into hard stones or solid iron that never crumbles into dust, for God still has the power to bring you forth.

phrases.translation: or whatever you think is harder to bring to life!” Then they will ask ˹you˺, “Who will bring us back ˹to life˺?” Say, “The One Who created you the first time.”
phrases.explanation: Or become whatever created thing seems even harder to bring to life in your minds, whether the heavens and earth, mountains, or even death itself. When they ask who could possibly bring them back to life, tell them: the very One who created you out of nothing the first time.

phrases.translation: They will then shake their heads at you and ask, “When will that be?” Say, “Perhaps it is soon!”
phrases.explanation: In mocking amazement they will shake their heads at you in derision and ask when this promised resurrection will ever take place. Answer their ridicule by warning them that perhaps the appointed time of their rising from the graves is already very near at hand.

phrases.translation: On the Day He will call you, you will ˹instantly˺ respond by praising Him, thinking you had remained ˹in the world˺ only for a little while
phrases.explanation: That resurrection will take place on the Day when God summons them from their graves and they instantly answer by His command and power, acknowledging His praise. Struck by the terror of that Day, they will think that they had remained in the world or in their graves for only a little while.

phrases.translation: Tell My ˹believing˺ servants to say only what is best.
phrases.explanation: Command the believing servants of God to say only what is best, gentlest, and most upright when conversing with one another or responding to provocation from polytheist opponents, pardoning harsh words, praying for God's mercy and forgiveness toward them, and speaking the truth without rudeness, anger, or abuse.

phrases.translation: Satan certainly seeks to sow discord among them. Satan is indeed a sworn enemy to humankind
phrases.explanation: Harsh speech must be avoided because Satan eagerly exploits angry words to sow discord, malice, and hostility among people and corrupt their brotherhood. Ever since he envied Adam and lured him out of the Garden, Satan has shown himself to be an open, sworn enemy to humankind.

phrases.translation: Your Lord knows you best. He may have mercy on you if He wills, or punish you if He wills.
phrases.explanation: Addressing the disbelievers, the verse reminds them that their Lord knows their hearts and destinies best. If He wills, He shows them mercy by guiding them to repentance and faith, and if He wills, He leaves them in their chosen disbelief to die upon polytheism and face punishment.

phrases.translation: We have not sent you ˹O Prophet˺ as a keeper over them
phrases.explanation: God consoles His Prophet by reminding him that he was not sent as a keeper, guardian, or warden responsible for compelling people to believe against their will. His sole duty is to deliver the message clearly, while guidance, mercy, and final reckoning belong entirely to God.

phrases.translation: Your Lord knows best all those in the heavens and the earth.
phrases.explanation: Your Lord knows best every inhabitant of the heavens and the earth and understands their true conditions, inner worth, and final destinies, for He is their Creator and Sustainer. The polytheists' arrogant disdain for humble believers or for your prophethood changes nothing before the One who governs all beings.

phrases.translation: And We have surely favoured some prophets above others, and to David We gave the Psalms
phrases.explanation: Just as God varies His gifts among creation, He has favored some prophets above others with distinct honors, taking Abraham as an intimate friend, speaking directly to Moses, granting Solomon an unmatched kingdom, forgiving Muhammad's past and future faults, and giving David the Psalms filled with praise and glorification.

phrases.translation: Say, ˹O Prophet,˺ “Invoke those you claim ˹to be divine˺ besides Him—they do not have the power to undo harm from you or transfer it ˹to someone else˺.”
phrases.explanation: Tell the polytheists who worship beings besides God, such as angels, Jesus, Ezra, or certain jinn: call upon those whom you claim to be divine when famine, sickness, or hardship strikes you, and see if they have any power to lift that affliction from you or transfer it onto someone else, for only the Creator possesses that power.

phrases.translation: ˹Even˺ the closest ˹to Allah˺ of those invoked would be seeking a way to their Lord, hoping for His mercy, and fearing His punishment. Indeed, your Lord’s torment is fearsome
phrases.explanation: The very beings whom the polytheists invoke, whether righteous servants like Jesus and Ezra, angels, or a group of jinn who accepted Islam while their human worshippers remained pagan, are themselves humble servants who compete in righteous deeds to seek nearness to their Lord, earnestly hoping for His mercy and fearing His fearsome torment.

phrases.translation: There is not a ˹wicked˺ society that We will not destroy or punish with a severe torment before the Day of Judgment. That is written in the Record
phrases.explanation: There is not a single wicked society on earth that God will not either destroy completely through death and ruin or afflict with a severe torment through war and calamity before the Day of Judgment arrives. This inescapable decree has already been written down in the Preserved Record.

phrases.translation: Nothing keeps Us from sending the ˹demanded˺ signs except that they had ˹already˺ been denied by earlier peoples.
phrases.explanation: When the Meccans demanded miracles like turning Mount Safa into gold, God explained that the only reason He held back such demanded signs was that earlier peoples had asked for them and then denied them once they appeared, bringing immediate annihilation upon themselves, whereas God knew some Meccans or their offspring would yet believe.

phrases.translation: And We gave Thamûd the she-camel as a clear sign, but they wrongfully rejected it. We only send the signs as a warning
phrases.explanation: Thus God gave the tribe of Thamud the miraculous she-camel they demanded as a clear, visible sign before their eyes, yet they wrongfully rejected it and hamstrung her, bringing destruction upon themselves. God sends such awesome signs only as a warning to strike fear into people so that they obey.

phrases.translation: And ˹remember, O Prophet˺ when We told you, “Certainly your Lord encompasses the people.”
phrases.explanation: Remember when God assured you that your Lord encompasses all people within His power and grasp, guarding and protecting you from the plots of the Quraysh so that they cannot kill you or stop you from proclaiming His message, and promising the eventual conquest of Mecca.

phrases.translation: And We have made what We brought you to see as well as the cursed tree ˹mentioned˺ in the Quran only as a test for the people. We keep warning them, but it only increases them greatly in defiance
phrases.explanation: The waking vision God brought His Prophet to see on the night journey to Jerusalem, along with the cursed Zaqqum tree mentioned in the Quran as growing in the bottom of Hell, was made only as a test that exposed scoffing hearts. Although God keeps warning them, their stubbornness only increases them in great defiance.

phrases.translation: And ˹remember˺ when We said to the angels, “Prostrate before Adam,” so they all did—but not Iblîs,
phrases.explanation: Remind the obstinate polytheists who follow Satan's footsteps of when God commanded the angels to prostrate in honor and respect before Adam, and all of the angels bowed in immediate obedience except Iblis, who refused out of envy, vanity, and arrogance toward the new creation.

phrases.translation: who protested, “Should I prostrate to the one You have created from mud?”
phrases.explanation: Looking down on Adam with foolish pride because he himself had been created from fire while Adam was formed from earth, Iblis protested to his Lord and asked scornfully how he could ever bow in prostration before a mortal creature whom God had fashioned out of humble mud and clay.

phrases.translation: Adding, “Do you see this one you honoured above me? If you delay my end until the Day of Judgment, I will certainly take hold of his descendants, except for a few.”
phrases.explanation: Questioning God's wisdom in honoring Adam above him, Iblis swore that if God delayed his end until the Day of Judgment, he would take hold of Adam's descendants, leading them around like an animal held by the bridle and uprooting them into ruin, except for a small band of sincere believers.

phrases.translation: Allah responded, “Be gone! Whoever of them follows you, Hell will surely be the reward for all of you—an ample reward
phrases.explanation: God answered Iblis by commanding him to be gone under the respite granted to him until the appointed time, while warning that for him and for every descendant of Adam who follows his lures and defies God, Hell will be their shared reward, an ample, complete, and unsparing recompense.

phrases.translation: And incite whoever you can of them with your voice, mobilize against them all your cavalry and infantry,
phrases.explanation: Continuing the stern challenge, God tells Iblis to incite and unsettle whomever he can with his voice, which early authorities explained as every call to sin or specifically idle entertainment, flute-playing, and song, and to mobilize against them all his cavalry and infantry, meaning every rider and foot soldier who marches in disobedience to God.

phrases.translation: manipulate them in their wealth and children, and make them promises.” But Satan promises them nothing but delusion
phrases.explanation: Let him manipulate them in their wealth through usury, unlawful gain, and livestock dedicated to idols, and in their children through adultery, burying infants alive, or naming them after false gods, and let him make them false promises. Yet Satan promises his followers nothing in the end except empty delusion.

phrases.translation: ˹Allah added,˺ “You will truly have no authority over My ˹faithful˺ servants.” And sufficient is your Lord as a Guardian
phrases.explanation: God declares to Iblis that over His faithful, believing servants who obey Him and resist temptation, Satan will never have any compelling authority or proof to force them into ruin. And your Lord alone suffices as a Guardian and Protector for those who place their trust in Him.

phrases.translation: It is your Lord Who steers the ships for you through the sea, so that you may seek His bounty. Surely He is ever Merciful to you
phrases.explanation: Turning back to the polytheists, the verse reminds them that their Lord is the One who gently steers the ships for them across the sea so that they can travel to distant lands for trade and seek His bounty. By making sea travel easy for them, He shows them immense mercy.

phrases.translation: When you are touched with hardship at sea, you ˹totally˺ forget all ˹the gods˺ you ˹normally˺ invoke, except Him.
phrases.explanation: Yet when a violent storm and mortal hardship strike them out at sea, all the idols and false gods they normally invoke vanish from their minds and are forgotten, and they cry out in desperate sincerity to God alone for rescue because they know none else can save them.

phrases.translation: But when He delivers you ˹safely˺ to shore, you turn away. Humankind is ever ungrateful
phrases.explanation: As soon as God answers their desperate plea and delivers them safely ashore on dry land, they turn away from pure devotion to Him alone and return to worshiping their false idols. Truly, unguided human nature is deeply ungrateful and quick to deny its Lord's favors.

phrases.translation: Do you feel secure that He will not cause the land to swallow you up, or unleash upon you a storm of stones? Then you will find none to protect you
phrases.explanation: Once you reach dry land and resume your ingratitude, do you really feel secure that God will not cause the shore itself to cave in and swallow you up, or unleash upon you a deadly storm of stones from the sky as He did to the people of Lot, leaving you with no protector to save you?

phrases.translation: Or do you feel secure that He will not send you back to sea once again, and send upon you a violent storm, drowning you for your denial? Then you will find none to avenge you against Us
phrases.explanation: Or do you feel secure that He will not send you back out to sea on another voyage and unleash against your ships a violent, shattering gale that splinters everything in its path, drowning you for your persistent denial, after which you will find no claimant or avenger to pursue Us on your behalf?

phrases.translation: Indeed, We have dignified the children of Adam, carried them on land and sea, granted them good and lawful provisions, and privileged them far above many of Our creatures
phrases.explanation: God has dignified the descendants of Adam with upright stature, reason, speech, mastery over other creatures, and eating with their hands, while carrying them on riding beasts across the land and in ships upon the sea, granting them good and lawful provisions, and privileging them far above many of His created beings.

phrases.translation: ˹Beware of˺ the Day We will summon every people with their leader.
phrases.explanation: Warn them of the Day of Judgment when God will summon every group of people along with their leader, which early authorities explained as their prophet, the scripture and law they followed, the leader who guided them in the world, or the written record of their own deeds.

phrases.translation: So whoever will be given their record in their right hand will read it ˹happily˺ and will not be wronged ˹even by the width of˺ the thread of a date stone
phrases.explanation: Those who are given their record of deeds in their right hand will read the good inscribed for them happily, while their forgiven sins pass unmentioned. They will not be wronged or have their reward diminished even by the width of the fine thread inside the groove of a date stone.

phrases.translation: But whoever is blind ˹to the truth˺ in this ˹world˺ will be blind in the Hereafter, and ˹even˺ far more astray from the ˹Right˺ Way
phrases.explanation: Whoever remains willfully blind in this worldly life to God's signs, blessings, and prophetic proofs will be raised even blinder in the Hereafter to any path of salvation, and far more astray from the Right Way because no chance of repentance or return remains for him.

phrases.translation: They definitely ˹thought they˺ were about to lure you away from what We have revealed to you ˹O Prophet˺, hoping that you would attribute something else to Us falsely—and then they would have certainly taken you as a close friend
phrases.explanation: The polytheists of Quraysh or Thaqif nearly succeeded in luring the Prophet away from parts of what God had revealed to him, hoping he would invent concessions in their favor, such as granting their shrines temporary immunity or praising their idols, so that they would gladly take him as a close friend and ally.

phrases.translation: Had We not made you steadfast, you probably would have inclined to them a little
phrases.explanation: Had God not made His Prophet's heart steadfast and safeguarded him through unfailing divine protection, he would almost have inclined to them a little out of his intense desire for his people to accept Islam, prompting him to pray that God never leave him to himself even for the blink of an eye.

phrases.translation: and then We truly would have made you taste double ˹punishment˺ both in this life and after death, and you would have found no helper against Us
phrases.explanation: God underscores the gravity of compromising revelation by declaring that if the Prophet had yielded to their pressure, He would have made him taste double the punishment of an ordinary disbeliever in this worldly life and double the punishment after death, with no helper able to defend him against God.

phrases.translation: They were about to intimidate you to drive you out of the land ˹of Mecca˺, but then they would not have survived after you ˹had left˺ except for a little while
phrases.explanation: The disbelievers plotted to intimidate the Prophet and drive him out of the land of Mecca. God warns that once a community actually expels its prophet, it would not survive in safety after his departure except for a little while before divine punishment or conquest overtakes it, as happened at Badr.

phrases.translation: ˹This has been˺ Our way with the messengers We sent before you. And you will never find any change in Our way
phrases.explanation: Destroying an arrogant nation shortly after it drives out its prophet has been God's unchanging way and established custom with all the communities to whom He sent messengers before Muhammad. You will never find any change, deviation, or alteration in that binding divine law across the ages.

phrases.translation: Observe the prayer from the decline of the sun until the darkness of the night and the dawn prayer, for certainly the dawn prayer is witnessed ˹by angels˺
phrases.explanation: Observe the prescribed prayers faithfully from the decline of the sun, which early authorities explained either as its passing the midday zenith for the noon and afternoon prayers or as its setting at dusk, until the darkness of night for the evening and night prayers, along with the dawn prayer witnessed by the angels of night and day.

phrases.translation: And rise at ˹the last˺ part of the night, offering additional prayers, so your Lord may raise you to a station of praise
phrases.explanation: And rise from sleep during part of the night to offer additional prayers with recitation of the Quran as a special devotion for you, so that your Lord may raise you on the Day of Judgment to a station of praise, the supreme station of intercession where all humanity will praise you.

phrases.translation: And say, “My Lord! Grant me an honourable entrance and an honourable exit and give me a supporting authority from Yourself.”
phrases.explanation: Pray to your Lord to grant you an honorable, truthful entrance and an honorable exit, which early authorities connected to leaving Mecca and entering Medina during the migration, entering and leaving the grave in peace, or every task undertaken for God, and to give you from Himself a victorious, supporting authority that establishes His religion.

phrases.translation: And declare, “The truth has come and falsehood has vanished. Indeed, falsehood is bound to vanish.”
phrases.explanation: And declare that the truth of the Quran, Islam, and God's promised victory has come, and that the falsehood of Satan and idol worship has vanished, for falsehood by its very nature cannot endure. When the Prophet entered Mecca at its conquest, he recited this verse while striking down the idols around the Kaaba.

phrases.translation: We send down the Quran as a healing and mercy for the believers, but it only increases the wrongdoers in loss
phrases.explanation: God sends down the Quran as a spiritual healing that cures hearts of doubt, ignorance, and error, and as a mercy for the believers who act upon its guidance. Yet for the polytheistic wrongdoers who reject each verse, it only increases them in ruin and loss as they pile denial upon denial.

phrases.translation: When We grant people Our favours, they turn away, acting arrogantly. But when touched with evil, they lose all hope
phrases.explanation: Whenever God grants ungrateful people His favors of health, safety, and abundant provision, they turn away from remembering Him and haughtily distance themselves from obedience. Yet as soon as hardship, poverty, or illness touches them, they lose all hope and sink into despair because they do not trust their Lord.

phrases.translation: Say, ˹O Prophet,˺ “Everyone acts in their own way. But your Lord knows best whose way is rightly guided.”
phrases.explanation: Tell the people that every person acts according to his own inner disposition, nature, intention, and chosen way of religion, whether righteous and obedient or corrupt and rebellious. Your Lord knows best whose way among you is genuinely rightly guided toward the truth and pleasing to Him.

phrases.translation: They ask you ˹O Prophet˺ about the spirit. Say, “Its nature is known only to my Lord, and you ˹O humanity˺ have been given but little knowledge.”
phrases.explanation: When Jewish rabbis or the Quraysh prompted by them asked the Prophet about the spirit, which early authorities explained as the breath of life in bodies, the angel Gabriel, or a mighty angel, God instructed him to reply that its true nature is known only to his Lord, and that all humanity has been given only a tiny measure of knowledge.

phrases.translation: If We willed, We could have certainly taken away what We have revealed to you ˹O Prophet˺—then you would find none to guarantee its return from Us—
phrases.explanation: God reminds His Prophet that all revelation depends entirely on His grace: if He willed, He could easily take away what He has revealed of the Quran by erasing it from hearts and written pages, and then you would find no protector or advocate able to guarantee its return from God.

phrases.translation: had it not been for the mercy of your Lord. Indeed, His favour upon you is immense
phrases.explanation: God has left the Quran preserved with you only out of the mercy of your Lord toward you and your community. Truly, His favor upon you is immense, for He chose you as the seal of His messengers, revealed His Book to you, and promised you the station of praise.

phrases.translation: Say, ˹O Prophet,˺ “If ˹all˺ humans and jinn were to come together to produce the equivalent of this Quran, they could not produce its equal, no matter how they supported each other.”
phrases.explanation: Answering critics who claimed they could compose something equal to the revelation, God commands the Prophet to declare that even if all human beings and all jinn came together to produce the equivalent of this Quran, they could never produce its equal, no matter how strongly they supported and backed one another.

phrases.translation: And We have truly set forth every ˹kind of˺ lesson for humanity in this Quran, yet most people persist in disbelief
phrases.explanation: In this Quran, God has truly set forth for humanity every kind of lesson, parable, proof, and warning so that they might reflect and follow the truth. Yet despite the clarity of these reminders, most people stubbornly refuse everything except ingratitude and persist in disbelief.

phrases.translation: They challenge ˹the Prophet˺, “We will never believe in you until you cause a spring to gush forth from the earth for us
phrases.explanation: Leaders of the Meccan polytheists challenged the Prophet in stubborn defiance, declaring that they would never believe in his message or accept his prophethood unless he split open the dry earth of Mecca before their eyes and caused a gushing spring of fresh water to flow for them.

phrases.translation: or until you have a garden of palm trees and vineyards, and cause rivers to flow abundantly in it
phrases.explanation: Continuing their arrogant demands, the Meccan leaders insisted that they would never believe in him until he possessed a lush garden of date palms and vineyards in their valley and caused rivers of water to burst forth and flow abundantly right through the midst of its trees.

phrases.translation: or cause the sky to fall upon us in pieces, as you have claimed, or bring Allah and the angels before us, face to face
phrases.explanation: Or, they mocked, he must cause the sky to fall down upon them in solid pieces of punishment, as he had warned God could do to them, or bring God Himself and the angels before them face to face so they could behold them directly.

phrases.translation: or until you have a house of gold, or you ascend into heaven—and even then we will not believe in your ascension until you bring down to us a book that we can read.”
phrases.explanation: Or he must own a house made of gold instead of living modestly, or climb a ladder up into heaven before their eyes, and even then they swore they would not believe in his ascension until he brought down a written book from God addressed to them that they could read.

phrases.translation: Say, “Glory be to my Lord! Am I not only a human messenger?”
phrases.explanation: God instructs His Prophet to reply by glorifying his Lord above being dictated to by His creatures, and by asking them whether he is anything more than a mortal human messenger who cannot perform miracles at his own whim, but only delivers the message God reveals.

phrases.translation: And nothing has prevented people from believing when guidance comes to them except their protest: “Has Allah sent a human as a messenger?”
phrases.explanation: Nothing has prevented the polytheists of Mecca and earlier nations from believing when clear guidance and proof came to them except their own ignorant protest and astonishment: how could God have sent an ordinary mortal human being like themselves as His messenger instead of an angel?

phrases.translation: Say, ˹O Prophet,˺ “Had there been angels walking the earth, well settled, We would have surely sent down for them an angel from heaven as a messenger.”
phrases.explanation: Answer their objection by explaining that a messenger is always sent from the same kind as those he addresses so they can behold and converse with him. Had there been angels walking the earth well settled as its inhabitants instead of humans, God would have sent down for them an angel from heaven as a messenger.

phrases.translation: Say, “Sufficient is Allah as a Witness between me and you. He is certainly All-Knowing, All-Seeing of His servants.”
phrases.explanation: Tell those who demand stubborn signs that God alone suffices as a righteous Witness and Judge between me and you, testifying that I have delivered His message truthfully. He is certainly All-Knowing and All-Seeing of His servants, fully aware of who is guided and who is obstinate.

phrases.translation: Whoever Allah guides is truly guided. And whoever He leaves to stray, you will find no guardians for them besides Him.
phrases.explanation: Whoever God guides to faith and truth is truly guided upon the straight path, whereas whoever God leaves to stray in his chosen disbelief will never find any guardians, allies, or protectors besides God to rescue him, defend him, or ward off torment when punishment arrives.

phrases.translation: And We will drag them on their faces on the Day of Judgment—deaf, dumb, and blind. Hell will be their home. Whenever it dies down, We will flare it up for them
phrases.explanation: On the Day of Judgment, God will drag them upon their faces to the gathering place, deaf, dumb, and blind to anything that could comfort or save them. Hell will be their permanent home, and whenever its flames die down after consuming their flesh, God flares the blaze up again for them.

phrases.translation: That is their reward for rejecting Our signs and asking ˹mockingly˺, “When we are reduced to bones and ashes, will we really be raised as a new creation?”
phrases.explanation: This dreadful gathering upon their faces and unrelenting fire is their just reward because they rejected God's signs and messengers in the world and asked mockingly how they could ever be raised up as a new creation after being reduced to decayed bones and ashes in their graves.

phrases.translation: Have they not realized that Allah, Who created the heavens and the earth, can ˹easily˺ re-create them?
phrases.explanation: Have those deniers not realized with the eyes of their hearts that the God who created the vast heavens and the earth out of nothing is easily able by that very same power to recreate human beings like them after they have decayed into dust?

phrases.translation: He has ˹already˺ set for them a time, about which there is no doubt. But the wrongdoers persist in denial
phrases.explanation: Moreover, God has already set for those deniers an appointed time for their death in this world and for their resurrection on the Day of Judgment, about which there is no doubt whatsoever. Even after seeing this decisive proof of divine power, the wrongdoers stubbornly persist in denial.

phrases.translation: Say ˹to them, O Prophet˺, “Even if you were to possess the ˹infinite˺ treasuries of my Lord’s mercy, then you would certainly withhold ˹them˺, fearing they would run out—for humankind is ever stingy!”
phrases.explanation: Tell the polytheists who demanded springs and golden palaces that even if they possessed the infinite treasuries of my Lord's mercy and provision, they would still withhold them and refuse to spend out of fear that their wealth would run out and leave them poor, for unguided humankind is ever stingy.

phrases.translation: We surely gave Moses nine clear signs. ˹You, O Prophet, can˺ ask the Children of Israel.
phrases.explanation: God gave Moses nine clear, unmistakable signs proving his prophethood, which early authorities identified as his staff, his radiant hand, the parting of the sea or loosening of his tongue, the years of drought and loss of fruits, the flood, the locusts, the lice, the frogs, and the blood, and the Prophet is told to ask the Children of Israel about them.

phrases.translation: When Moses came to them, Pharaoh said to him, “I really think that you, O Moses, are bewitched.”
phrases.explanation: When Moses came to Pharaoh and his people in Egypt with those nine clear signs, Pharaoh rejected them out of arrogance and responded to him with the exact same insult that the Quraysh leveled against Muhammad, claiming that Moses was merely a man bewitched by magic.

phrases.translation: Moses replied, “You know well that none has sent these ˹signs˺ down except the Lord of the heavens and the earth as insights. And I really think that you, O Pharaoh, are doomed.”
phrases.explanation: Moses replied directly to Pharaoh, or in a variant reading declared of himself, that Pharaoh knew well in his heart that none had sent down these nine signs except the Lord of the heavens and the earth as clear insights and proofs, though he denied them out of arrogance, and Moses declared that Pharaoh was surely doomed to ruin.

phrases.translation: So Pharaoh wanted to scare the Israelites out of the land ˹of Egypt˺, but We drowned him and all of those with him
phrases.explanation: Just as the Quraysh plotted to drive Muhammad out of Mecca, Pharaoh wanted to scare Moses and the Israelites out of the land of Egypt or wipe them out completely, so God drowned Pharaoh and all of the hosts who marched with him together in the sea.

phrases.translation: And We said to the Children of Israel after Pharaoh, “Reside in the land, but when the promise of the Hereafter comes to pass, We will bring you all together.”
phrases.explanation: After drowning Pharaoh, God told the Children of Israel to reside safely in the land of Syria and Egypt from which Pharaoh had tried to expel them, and declared that when the promised Hour of the Hereafter comes to pass, He will bring both believers and disbelievers forth from their graves mingled together in one great gathering.

phrases.translation: We have sent down the Quran in truth, and with the truth it has come down. We have sent you ˹O Prophet˺ only as a deliverer of good news and a warner
phrases.explanation: With truth, justice, and unassailable reality God has sent down this Quran from Himself, and with that same truth it has come down intact through Gabriel to Muhammad. And God sent His Prophet not to force people to believe, but only as a deliverer of good news of Paradise and a warner of the Fire.

phrases.translation: ˹It is˺ a Quran We have revealed in stages so that you may recite it to people at a deliberate pace. And We have sent it down in successive revelations
phrases.explanation: God made the Quran distinct and clear in its rulings, or in a variant reading revealed it in separate stages, so that the Prophet might recite it to people at a deliberate, measured pace that they could understand and retain, sending it down in successive revelations according to events and needs.

phrases.translation: Say, ˹O Prophet,˺ “Believe in this ˹Quran˺, or do not.
phrases.explanation: Tell the stubborn deniers who demand capricious miracles before accepting the revelation, even though humans and jinn together could never match it: whether you choose to believe in this Quran or refuse to believe in it, your faith adds nothing to the treasuries of God's mercy and your disbelief diminishes nothing from His kingdom.

phrases.translation: Indeed, when it is recited to those who were gifted with knowledge before it ˹was revealed˺, they fall upon their faces in prostration
phrases.explanation: Indeed, when this Quran is recited to those upright scholars among the People of the Book who were gifted with scriptural knowledge before it was revealed, they immediately recognize its truth as coming from God and fall down upon their faces and chins in humble prostration.

phrases.translation: and say, ‘Glory be to our Lord! Surely the promise of our Lord has been fulfilled.’
phrases.explanation: While prostrating upon their faces, those knowledgeable believers say: Glory be to our Lord above every false claim, for surely the promise of our Lord foretold in the earlier scriptures, both the coming of Muhammad with the Quran and the certainty of the Resurrection, has been fulfilled.

phrases.translation: And they fall down upon their faces weeping, and it increases them in humility.”
phrases.explanation: Overwhelmed by awe and reverence for God, those knowledgeable believers among the People of the Book fall down upon their faces weeping as they listen to the recited verses of the Quran, and its admonitions, lessons, and promises continually increase them in deep humility, obedience, and submissiveness before their Lord.

phrases.translation: Say, ˹O Prophet,˺ “Call upon Allah or call upon the Most Compassionate—whichever you call, He has the Most Beautiful Names.”
phrases.explanation: When the polytheists heard the Prophet pray in prostration calling out 'O Allah, O Most Compassionate,' they claimed he was invoking two gods. God instructed him to say that whether you call upon Him as Allah or as the Most Compassionate, both refer to the One Lord to whom belong the Most Beautiful Names.

phrases.translation: Do not recite your prayers too loudly or silently, but seek a way between
phrases.explanation: And do not recite your prayers or supplications in Mecca so loudly that the polytheists hear and revile the Quran and the One who revealed it, nor so silently that your companions behind you cannot hear and learn from you, but seek a moderate middle way between the two.

phrases.translation: And say, “All praise is for Allah, Who has never had ˹any˺ offspring; nor does He have a partner in ˹governing˺ the kingdom; nor is He pathetic, needing a protector. And revere Him immensely.”
phrases.explanation: Conclude by praising God and refuting every false belief of the Christians, Jews, Magians, and Arab polytheists: all praise belongs to God, who has never taken any offspring, who has no partner sharing in governing His kingdom, and who is never weak or pathetic so as to need a protector, and revere and magnify Him immensely.
